title: pennsylvania-lpm Policy Timeline Event Record
description: A single dated (or date-ranged) event in Pennsylvania's K-12 science-curriculum policy history -- past, current, or planned/future. Unlike nys_lp's single reform thread (graduation measures), Pennsylvania's evolution-education history runs through a single, intensely documented episode -- a school district's own policy, a six-week federal trial, and a school-board election, all within about 14 months of 2004-2005 -- which is exactly the shape eventType's court-ruling/school-board-action values (inherited unchanged from florida-lpm, where they were added for a differently-shaped recurring state-level pattern) were built to capture. The point of a machine-readable timeline is to let a policy brief programmatically ask 'what's already decided vs. still in motion' rather than re-deriving it from prose each time. Same base shape as deutsche_lp's/nys_lp's/india-lpm's/florida-lpm's policy-timeline-event.schema.json.

eventType.description: The four values added for florida-lpm (court-ruling, public-hearing, school-board-action, advocacy-campaign), inherited here unchanged, turn out to fit Pennsylvania's own history just as directly -- 'court-ruling' is literally the Kitzmiller v. Dover ruling itself, and 'school-board-action' is literally Dover Area School District's October 2004 policy vote. 'election' is new here: a public vote for an office (a school-board seat, a state legislative seat) where the curriculum dispute itself was a defining issue in the race -- Dover's November 2005 election, which ousted all eight pro-intelligent-design board members before the ruling even came down, is exactly this and fits none of the existing values (it is voters acting, not a board's own action). 'court-ruling' = a judicial decision (e.g. a federal court ruling on an Establishment Clause challenge). 'public-hearing' = a formal public-comment session on proposed standards/rules. 'school-board-action' = a vote or resolution by a sub-state board (a county/district school board), as distinct from 'framework-adopted' which is reserved for the state-level governing board. 'advocacy-campaign' = a named, organized push by a non-governmental actor (an advocacy body, think tank, or grassroots group) that is itself the notable event, not a government action.

dateGranularity.description: Some Pennsylvania administrative dates are given as a school year (e.g. '2020-21') rather than a calendar date; record dateStart as the school year's start (e.g. 2020-08-01) and note the granularity here.

temporalStatus.description: Relative to this record's own provenance.date -- not auto-derived, since 'current' drifts.

partOf.description: Id of a broader event/programme this is one milestone of, if any (e.g. a specific public-comment hearing that is part of the overall 2026 proposed-standards review process).

accessTier.description: How much of the underlying source this record actually keeps, chosen per-source based on what's legally safe to redistribute for this document -- not one all-or-nothing repo-wide rule. Relevant here because `description` sometimes embeds a substantial verbatim quotation (e.g. a State Board of Education statement, or a news report's headline/lede). 'full-text-stored' = description reproduces the source substantially verbatim. 'excerpt-only' = description contains only short, clearly-bounded quotations -- the de facto tier this repo has used by default. 'summary-only' = description is paraphrase only, no verbatim text. 'citation-only' = only sourceUrl is kept, no text from the source at all. Optional; a record without this field predates founding and should be treated as 'excerpt-only' at most until reviewed. Identical field to deutsche_lp's/nys_lp's/india-lpm's policy-timeline-event.schema.json.

licenseOrRightsNote.description: The legal basis for storing this source at the accessTier chosen above, e.g. 'Pennsylvania state-government publications and State Board of Education rule text are public records and not subject to copyright', 'a federal court's own published opinion (Kitzmiller v. Dover, 400 F. Supp. 2d 707) is a public judicial record', or 'news-outlet reporting -- headline/short excerpt only, fair-use/citation basis, full article not reproduced'. Mirrors OpenLPM's standards_documents.license_or_rights_note field (openlpm migration 019) for ecosystem-wide naming consistency.
